headline: MSCI shock, a soft auction and a record-low rupiah push the IGSYC 10Y to 7.63% (+4.5bp): up 52bp in October, near its highest since 2020
summary: INDOGBs sold off again on Friday, led by the belly: on PHEI's IGSYC curve the 1Y rose 6.6bp to 6.862%, the 2Y 4.7bp to 7.010%, the 5Y 7.8bp to 7.522% and the 10Y 4.5bp to 7.628%, and the curve is flat at 7.629% from 13 years out. The 10Y ends October 52bp higher and sits at the top of its 1-year range (99th percentile), about 150bp above where 2026 began. This is an Indonesia-specific sell-off, not a global one: US Treasuries rallied over the same four weeks. Government sukuk held up better (the fitted PBS 10Y is about 10bp through IGSYC), while corporate credit is wide but orderly, with AAA 3Y 53bp over IGSYC.
drivers: MSCI standalone threat and the foreign exit

MSCI opened a consultation on Oct 15 to move Indonesia from Emerging Markets to a Standalone market, harsher than the Frontier downgrade it had threatened in January; the JCI fell 11.6% on Oct 16 and closed the month at 5,057, 44% below its Jan 15 peak of 9,075. Banks estimate US$3–4.8bn of passive selling and up to US$15bn from active funds, with a final decision due by Jun 30, 2027. Foreigners kept selling stocks all week (about Rp1.1tn net on Thursday, mostly the big banks), and bonds followed once the rupiah gave way.
Rupiah at record lows, BI defending with the corridor

JISDOR fixed at 18,138 on Oct 30, near the weakest on record and about 8% down this year. On Oct 21 BI held the BI-Rate at 5.75% but lifted the deposit facility to 5.00% and widened DNDF and hedging incentives, a defensive move that pushed the short end up: the IGSYC 1Y is 111bp over the BI-Rate. Indonesia's 5Y CDS rose from about 92bp on Oct 14 to 106bp on Oct 26.

The Oct 27 SUN auction drew only Rp31.1tn of bids for Rp20.65tn awarded, and the new 10Y FR0111 cleared at a 7.54% average, 30bp higher in two weeks. The 2026 deficit outlook was raised to 2.85% of GDP from 2.68%, with about Rp302tn of net SBN still to issue after Rp497.5tn (62%) by September, and the 10Y now trades about 70bp above the budget's 6.9% assumption. Retail demand is the bright spot: Rp17tn of SBR015 savings bonds sold.
US Treasuries are not the driver

The US 10Y fell 26bp over the last four weeks while the INDOGB 10Y rose 47bp; the 26-week weekly beta is −0.06, so essentially all of October's move is local. The daily beta to the overnight US move has dropped to 0.07 over 60 days from 0.29 over the year. Friday's New York session took the US 10Y down 4bp, worth only about −1bp for INDOGBs at the 1-year beta, so don't expect much help from Treasuries until local flows calm.
data: SUN auction (Oct 27)
Bids Rp31.09tn, awarded Rp20.65tn; FR0111 10Y average 7.54%
Weak cover for a supply-heavy quarter. The Ministry took less than it could, but the 30bp jump in the 10Y award in two weeks sets a higher floor for secondary yields.
SBR015 retail savings bond (Oct 27)
Rp17.0tn sold (T2 Rp13.6tn, T4 Rp3.4tn)
Strong household demand gives the Ministry a cushion outside the auctions and takes some pressure off the 2–4Y sector.
2026 budget outlook (late Oct)
Deficit 2.85% of GDP (budget 2.68%); net SBN Rp497.5tn (62.2%) issued by Sep
About Rp302tn still to raise in Q4 into a market with foreign demand fading: a supply overhang that weighs most on the long end.
BI board meeting (Oct 21)
BI-Rate 5.75% (hold, 100bp of hikes this year); deposit facility 5.00% (up); lending facility 6.50%
A rupiah-defence move: tighter liquidity at the very front without a headline hike. A BI-Rate hike in November is possible if JISDOR breaks higher.
MSCI market classification (Oct 15)
Consultation to move Indonesia from EM to Standalone; feedback by Apr 30, 2027; decision by Jun 30, 2027
Long-dated overhang for foreign equity money; it hits the rupiah first and bonds through the currency and risk premium.
September CPI (Oct 1)
Inside BI's 1.5–3.5% target but rising on food; a weaker rupiah adds imported inflation risk. October CPI is forecast near 3.19%.
External position (Q2 / end-Sep)
Current account −US$12.5bn (−3.3% of GDP); reserves US$146.3bn
A wider current-account gap makes the rupiah more dependent on portfolio inflows, which is exactly what is reversing.
view: The market is pricing a foreign exit, not a BI easing or a global rates move, and that keeps duration risk one-sided for now: the Bond Flow Signal reads −0.69 (sell-off) for a fifth week, driven by the JCI slump and the 10Y's own momentum, and the call has been right so far (+47bp since Oct 2). The quant record argues for patience rather than conviction: the signal is only modestly positive since 2022 (Sharpe 0.18), but since September 2024, when foreign flows took over, it scores 0.79 outright and 1.04 against Treasuries, and its sell-off calls are right 54% of the time. Value is building: INDOGBs yield 265bp over Treasuries (85th percentile of the year) and the spread part of the signal is already bond-bullish. I expect the 10Y to range 7.45–7.90% over the next two weeks, with the upside tested if JISDOR breaks 18,300 or BI has to hike. I would stay underweight 10Y and longer until the rupiah stabilises and the signal climbs back above −0.5, express curve views through a 10s20s steepener given the long-end supply, and switch rich PBS sukuk into FR series where mandates allow; a Treasury hedge adds little while the beta is near zero.

buckets.name: Front end 1–2Y vs BI-Rate
buckets.why: The IGSYC 1Y at 6.862% is 111bp over the 5.75% BI-Rate and about 186bp over the new 5.00% deposit facility, so it already prices tighter liquidity and some chance of another hike. The 2Y at 7.010% is only 15bp above the 1Y. PHEI history for these tenors starts this week, so the meter rests on two days and the call relies on the policy spread.
buckets.call: Neutral. Add 1–2Y only if the 1Y reaches 7.10% (a hike fully priced) or if the rupiah stabilises below 18,000; avoid chasing below 6.70%.

buckets.name: Belly 5Y (FR0109)
buckets.why: The 5Y led Friday's sell-off (+7.8bp to 7.522%), and the FR0109 benchmark (4.4Y) is the cheapest of the four FR benchmarks against the curve at 7.537%, about 8bp above IGSYC at its term. The belly carries the best carry and roll on a curve that is steep to 5Y and flat beyond, and retail money (SBR, ORI) supports it.
buckets.call: Start buying FR0109 near 7.55–7.60% once JISDOR holds below 18,200 for three sessions; target 7.30%, stop 7.80%.

buckets.name: 10Y outright
buckets.why: The 10Y at 7.628% is at the 99th percentile of its 1-year range (average 6.72%), 52bp higher in October and about 70bp above the budget assumption. It is cheap on history and on the 265bp spread to Treasuries, but the flow signal still reads sell-off, the auction cover was thin and Q4 supply is heavy.
buckets.call: Stay underweight; turn neutral when the flow signal rises above −0.5 or the 10Y fails twice at 7.75–7.80%. A tactical long only above 7.85% with a stop at 8.05%.

buckets.name: 10s20s curve (FR0108 vs FR0107)
buckets.why: IGSYC is flat past 13 years (10s20s near 0bp), which leaves no term premium for Rp302tn of remaining supply. The benchmarks already disagree with the flat curve: FR0107 (18.8Y) yields 7.705%, 7.8bp over FR0108 (9.5Y) at 7.627% and 7.6bp cheap to IGSYC. Long-end supply usually steepens the curve as the quarter goes on.
buckets.call: Steepener: buy FR0108, sell FR0107 duration-weighted at a 7.8bp spread; target 18bp, stop 2bp.

buckets.name: PBS sukuk vs FR
buckets.why: The fitted PBS curve sits about 10bp through IGSYC at 10Y: PBS034 (12.6Y) is 11.9bp rich and PBS038 (23.1Y) 12.5bp rich, because sharia funds and Islamic banks must hold them and they have not sold. PBS030 at the front is close to fair (−3bp). The fit rests on only four PBS series, so treat the level with care.
buckets.call: Where mandates allow, switch PBS034/PBS038 into FR0106/FR0107 for about 15–20bp of pick-up; reverse when the rich-up narrows to 3bp.

buckets.name: Corporate credit (AAA 3Y)
buckets.why: PHEI's AAA 3Y curve is 53bp over IGSYC and AA 82bp, normal for Indonesia; the stress is lower down, with BBB 266bp over AA. Corporate spreads have not blown out the way sovereign yields have, because local banks and insurers dominate the buyer base.
buckets.call: Hold AAA/AA; add only if AAA 3Y widens past 70bp. Avoid BBB until the rupiah stabilises.

watch: Next: October CPI (Mon Nov 2, f 3.19%) and the IDX trading reforms taking effect the same day, Q3 GDP (around Nov 5), October FX reserves (around Nov 6), the next SUN auction in mid-November and BI's November board meeting; in the US, payrolls and Fed speakers. JISDOR 18,300 is the line that would force BI's hand.
sources: IDN Financials (bond yields and auction, Oct 29)
CNBC Indonesia (SBN 10Y at a six-year high, Oct 29)
